newsitem.title: USA: White House hails Mexico's drug reorganization.
newsitem.headline: White House hails Mexico's drug reorganization.

text.p: The White House on Thursday welcomed Mexico's decision to dismantle its scandal-marred anti-drug agency and replace it with a new body of trained agents who be screened on a regular basis.
"It's a positive and encouraging development taken independently by the government of Mexico," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
Presidential counselor Thomas "Mack" McLarty, the White House coordinator for U.S. policy toward Latin America, said the move showed Mexico "has exhibited the will to fight against drug traffickers."

"President (Ernesto) Zedillo said in 1994 that the number one national security threat to Mexico was narcotics and narcotics trafficking," McLarty said. "I think there's clearly a belief and strong feeling on the part of the Mexican people that this is a serious, very, very serious and concerning problem that must be addressed."

McLarty spoke with a group of reporters at the National Press Club one day after Mexican Attorney General Jorge Madrazo Cuellar announced that the new agency, the Special Prosecutor's Office for Crimes Against Health, would begin work immediately.
Drug offenses are termed crimes against health in Mexico.

The new agency replaces the National Institute for Drug Combat (INCD), which fell under a cloud when its chief, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, was arrested in February and charged with taking bribes from Mexico's most wanted drug lord, Amado Carrillo Fuentes.
The reorganization came five days before President Bill Clinton was due to arrive in Mexico for a visit that will include discussions on fighting drugs.

Washington has applied heavy pressure on Mexico in recent years to root out drug corruption and stop narcotics smuggling across the border.
